William Wentworth: Australian statesman, writer and explorer.

In what year was HIV/AIDS discovered?
HIV/AIDS: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system.
In what year was COVID-19 discovered?
COVID-19: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2.
Mannitol: Pfizer. Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication.
Which country is Bombardier Global Express from?

Special relativity: Albert Einstein. In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon dioxide?
Carbon dioxide: Jan Baptist van Helmont. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Who is credited with discovering Calcium?
Calcium: Humphry Davy. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Sitting atop the kidneys, this pair of endocrine glands produces hormones including adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol. What organ is it?
Adrenal gland (also known as suprarenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.
Its type species, a common freshwater organism constantly studied in classrooms and labs, lends its name to an entire genus of shape-changing single-celled organisms — what's the genus?
Amoeba (genus) is a genus of single-celled amoeboids in the family Amoebidae.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
From starch that stores energy to the cellulose that stiffens plants and the chitin in insect shells, this biomolecule family is essentially sugars and their derivatives — what is it?
Carbohydrate is a sugar (saccharide) or a sugar derivative.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

Produced by a mammal's mammary glands in the first days after birth, this antibody-rich milk helps protect newborns like calves and human infants from infection before regular milk takes over — which substance?
Colostrum (from Latin, of unknown origin), also known as foremilk, is the milk expressed by the mammary glands of a female mammal during the first few days following delivery of the newborn.
Mostly aquatic mandibulate arthropods, this group spans shrimp, crayfish, copepods, and barnacles — and modern science now files insects in alongside them — what are they?
Crustacean (from Latin word "crustacea" meaning: "those with shells" or "crusted ones") are mandibulate arthropods that are traditionally a part of the paraphyletic subphylum Crustacea.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.
This is the only surviving member of its order, the Proboscidea, and its tusks are actually overgrown incisor teeth used as both weapons and tools — what animal is it?
Elephant are the largest living land animals.
This ground-nesting songbird of Europe and the Palearctic sings its signature tune while hovering high over farmland and heath, and now also breeds in Australia and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
This genus in the rose family includes more than 20 species prized for their sweet-to-tart edible fruits, with domestic hybrids grown worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Fragaria is a genus of flowering plants in the rose family, Rosaceae, commonly known as strawberries for their edible fruits.
Before he founded a piece of the U.S. aircraft industry, this pioneer set an unofficial world speed record astride a V8-powered motorcycle that stood unbroken until 1911. Who was he?

Caused by a group of enteroviruses, this common infection opens with a fever and then sprinkles blistering spots on exactly the three body parts named in its label. What is it?
Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common infection caused by a group of enteroviruses. It typically begins with a fever and feeling generally unwell.
This small rodent, with a pointed snout and a long, nearly hairless tail, has thrived by living alongside humans to the point that truly wild populations are now rare — what animal is it?
House mouse (Mus musculus) is a small mammal of the rodent family Muridae, characteristically having a pointed snout, large rounded ears, and a long and almost hairless tail.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Known as the sunroot or earth apple, this central-North-American member of the sunflower family is cultivated for its tuber rather than its bloom — what is it?
Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America.
This American biologist and one-time Communist Party member had four husbands, the last being the physicist who led Los Alamos — who was she?
Kitty Oppenheimer (ne Puening; August 8, 1910 - October 27, 1972) was an American biologist, botanist, and a member of the Communist Party of America until leaving in the 1930s.
Viruses muddy its definition, and it might exist beyond Earth in unfamiliar forms — but on this planet it fills air, water and soil, even harsh niches of extremophiles. What is it?
Life is the capacity, in matter, for processes such as cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, cell growth, adaptation, response to stimuli, and reproduction.
This alpha-amino acid, a building block for many proteins, carries a side chain that stays partially charged at the body's normal pH, classifying it among the basic amino acids — what is it?
Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an -amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

These aquatic insects carry ancient traits from the first flying insects — long tails and wings that won't fold flat — and their water-dwelling young are a living signal of clean, unpolluted streams; what bug is this?
Mayfly (also up-winged flies or up-wing flies, or drake-flies in the UK; shadflies or fishflies in northern U.S.

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.

This genus of fragrant flowering shrubs, native to Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean, is widely grown as an ornamental in Hawaii and in desert climates of the Arabian Peninsula — name the genus?
Plumeria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.
This Eurasian fruit tree, also called the cherry plum, is believed to be one of the ancestral parents of the plum we cultivate today — what species is it?
Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum.
This biological process by which new organisms are produced from parents comes in two forms — one requiring a single organism, the other requiring two. What is it?
Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms - offspring - are produced from their parent or parents.

Originally conceived in the 1960s as a jet trainer before evolving into a supersonic strike aircraft, this joint British-French warplane — retired by both original operators — remains in service only with the Indian Air Force. Name it?
SEPECAT Jaguar is a British-French supersonic jet attack aircraft originally used by the British Royal Air Force and the French Air Force in the close air support and nuclear strike role.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
Native to a swath from Ireland to southern China, this aromatic herb is used to flavor food and herbal teas, and its extracted oil serves as both a flavoring and a scent — what is it?

Spearmint (Mentha spicata), also known as garden mint, common mint, lamb mint and mackerel mint, is native to Europe and southern temperate Asia, extending from Ireland in the west to southern China in the east.
This Chinese physician and revolutionary led the 1911 Revolution, overthrew the Qing dynasty, and founded the Republic of China as its first president. Who was he?
Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 - 12 March 1925) was a Chinese physician, revolutionary and political philosopher who founded the Republic of China (ROC) and the Kuomintang (KMT).
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Native to Central and South America but now found in sub-Saharan Africa, which parasitic flea burrows into skin to cause the condition tungiasis?
Tunga penetrans is a species of flea also known as the jigger, jigger flea, chigoe, chigo, chigoe flea, chigo flea, nigua, sand flea, or burrowing flea.

Manufactured under license by both Goodyear and Brewster during World War II, this American carrier-based fighter aircraft became one of the most capable fighter-bombers of the war and later saw service in Korea — which aircraft?
Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War.
Also called humped cattle for the fatty growth on its shoulders, this South Asian breed group is used for everything from plowing to dairy, and even kept as pets in miniature form — what is it?
Zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.
Located behind the nasal cavity where the nose meets the throat, which mass of lymphoid tissue is also known as the pharyngeal tonsil?
Adenoid: Type of tonsil. The adenoid, also known as the pharyngeal tonsil, or nasopharyngeal tonsil is the superior-most of the tonsils.

Capable of constantly changing its shape by extending and retracting temporary 'false feet,' this single-celled organism turns up across nearly every branch of the eukaryotic tree of life — what is it?
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.

Among the first life forms on Earth and typically just a few micrometres long, these single-celled prokaryotes thrive everywhere from hot springs to radioactive waste and drive the putrefaction stage of decay — what are they?

Betelgeuse: Red supergiant star in the constellation Orion. It is usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky and, after Rigel, the second brightest in its constellation.

Commonly called the Triple Seven, this American wide-body airliner is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airplane. It was designed to bridge the gap between the twin-engined 767 and quad-engined 747. What is it?

Brown rat: Species of common rat. One of the largest muroids, it is a brown or grey rodent with a body length of up to 28 cm (11 in) long, and a tail slightly shorter than that.
White, green, oolong, and black tea all come from the same evergreen shrub, simply processed to different levels of oxidation — name the plant species?
Camellia sinensis: Species of evergreen shrub. Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Native to the rainforests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this flightless ratite is the fourth-tallest and third-heaviest living bird, trailing only the ostriches and the emu?
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.

Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.

Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)

Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.
Closely related to the llama, this wild South American camelid shares its range with a higher-altitude cousin, the vicuña — what is it?

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'handy man' for its toolmaking, this archaic human species lived in East and South Africa as far back as 2.4 million years ago — which species?
Homo habilis: Archaic human species from 2.4 to 1.65 mya.
Formed when chlorine dissolves in water, this compound is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions — and your own white blood cells make it to fight off invading germs. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid: Chemical compound. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.

Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
The offspring of a male lion and a female tiger, which hybrid cat is the largest of all living felines and — unlike its reverse-cross cousin — grows larger than either parent?
Liger: Lion and tigress hybrid. The liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'tree of death' and 'beach apple,' this small-fruited tropical tree oozes a milky sap so toxic it can blister skin on contact — which tree?
Manchineel: Poisonous plant from tropical North and South America.

This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?

Monitor lizard: Genus of reptiles. Monitor lizards are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
A pale-blue gas with a chlorine-like pungent odour, this unstable three-atom cousin of oxygen forms by UV light and electrical discharges and shields us high in the stratosphere — what is it?
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
With a distinctive pale eye and grey nape against black plumage, this small, gregarious member of the crow family was first formally described by Linnaeus — name the bird?
Western jackdaw: Species of bird in the crow family Corvidae.
Also called the pikeperch, this ray-finned game fish native to western Eurasian waters is the type species that gave its whole genus a name — which fish?
Zander: Species of fish. The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
What is the chemical symbol for sulfur?
The symbol for sulfur is S. Sulfur, also spelled as sulphur, is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
What is the chemical symbol for rubidium?
The symbol for rubidium is Rb. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
